title: Style Templates on Lightning Maps (Beta)
summary: Org-level map style templates: where the entry points live, how an ArcGIS-sourced layer differs from a templated one, the attribute → style → options editor modelled on Esri's Styles pane, status-based icon colouring and a switchable icon library.
notes: Colours are chosen by name and swatch — “Violet Mid”, “Brand Blue”. Token codes only appear under Advanced → Developer reference.
Advanced holds the precise settings: opacity slider, contrast points against both basemaps, and a custom hex.
Colour ramp shows which one is Applied, and flips to “Custom” the moment you change a single class by hand.
Symbol style is geometry-aware and scoped to the class named in its header — line pattern + width on segments, shape + size + glyph on structures, fill on polygons. Every control repaints the map.
Every change repaints the map live. Opening the editor pauses the status overlay so you can actually see template colours — there is a one-click Show status to flip back.
Left panel scrolls; the map does not. Wheel / drag / double-click / arrow keys zoom and pan, and symbols hold constant screen size.
Layer card “…” → Style Layer. Templates tab has New, sortable columns and per-row actions.
Icon glyphs are stand-ins drawn for the mock, not licensed Calcite/SLDS/FontAwesome/Maki assets.
